research_question: Can one arm-blind, non-promoting Candidate Information-Set Reviewer call distinguish optimize-only semantic projection from predicates directly grounded in public task evidence before any Worker dispatch?

setup_failure.failure: The rootless runtime virtual environment did not include the optional openai package required by the first runner implementation.
setup_failure.scientific_interpretation: Infrastructure-only setup failure; not a Reviewer outcome.
setup_failure.repair: The runner was changed to use the Python standard-library HTTP client for the bounded OpenRouter request, then the same frozen plan and input were rerun.

retained_conclusion: One bounded arm-blind Reviewer call matched all five predeclared semantic-provenance verdicts, passed candidate-claim coverage, returned overall REJECT, respected zero-Worker and zero-promotion authority, and left no runtime residue.

claim_boundary.supported: Single-call bounded semantic discrimination on one synthetic mixed fixture, schema compliance, complete declared-claim coverage, exact predeclared verdict match, authority compliance, request accounting, and cleanup.
claim_boundary.not_supported: Reviewer infallibility, population precision or recall, recovery or reauthorization of any of the six contaminated candidates, candidate promotion, benchmark gain, or main-experiment readiness.
claim_boundary.main_readiness: NO-GO until the Reviewer is wired into the controller as a mandatory pre-Worker gate and one fresh public-only candidate passes that gate and obtains a retained official gain with a blind Worker.
